paper.title: More Adaptive Algorithms for Adversarial Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: combinatorial bandit problem with semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: action set X subset of {0,1}^K, K_0 = max number of arms in an action
settings.definition_quote: In each round, the learner selects a subset of arms, denoted by a binary vector $b_t$ from a predefined action set $\mathcal{X}\subseteq \{0,1\}^K$, and suffers loss $b_t^\top \ell_t$, where $\ell_t \in [-1,1]^K$ is a loss vector decided by an adversary. ... we assume that the adversary is oblivious

In the special case of multi-armed bandit, the action set $\mathcal{X}$ is $\{\mathbf{e}_1, \mathbf{e}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{e}_K\}$ ... the learner picks one arm $i_t \in [K]$ ... and receives the loss $\ell_{t,i_t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic setting with fixed gap (adapting to stochastic bandits)
unmapped: losses random but neither independent nor identically distributed; there is an arm a* whose conditional expected loss is smaller than every other arm's by a fixed gap Delta at every round (includes i.i.d. MAB as special case)
regret is with respect to the empirically best arm, in expectation over losses
settings.definition_quote: there exists an arm $a^*$ and some fixed gap $\Delta > 0$ such that $\mathbb{E}_{\ell_t}\left[\ell_{t,i}-\ell_{t,a^*} | \ell_1, \ldots, \ell_{t-1}\right]\geq \Delta$ for all $i \neq a^*$ and $t\in[T]$.

settings.name_in_paper: two-player zero-sum game with bandit feedback
unmapped: objective is convergence of average strategies to Nash equilibrium value; both players run the algorithm (self-play)
feedback is expected loss of own realized action over opponent's mixed strategy
game matrix G in [-1,1]^{M x N}
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, Player 1 randomly picks a row $i_t \sim x_t$ ... while Player 2 randomly picks a column $j_t \sim y_t$ ... we consider a setting where the feedbacks are the scalar values $\mathbf{e}_{i_t}^\top Gy_t$ and $x_t^\top G\mathbf{e}_{j_t}$ respectively

symbols.E_err: E[sum_t sum_{i in b*} (l_{t,i} - m_{t,i})^2], squared prediction error on comparator's arms
symbols.K_0: max number of arms in an action

source.label: cor:clear_corollary
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with $a_{t,i}=6\eta_{t,i}w_{t,i}(\hat{\ell}_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2$, any $m_{t,i} \in [-1, 1]$, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta \leq \frac{1}{162K_0}$ enjoys the following regret bound: $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T] \leq \frac{K\ln T}{\eta} + 6\eta\mathbb{E}[...] +\mathcal{O}(K_0)$

results.notes: Only the additive K_0 term is in O(); first two terms exact. Numbering guessed (shares counter with theorems).

symbols.Q_star: unnormalized variance of best arm's losses, sum_t (l_{t,i*} - mu_{T,i*})^2

extra_assumptions: uses reservoir sampling of Hazan & Kale

source.label: cor:variance_bound
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with reservoir sampling~\citep{hazan2011better}, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{162}$ guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]= \mathcal{O}(\frac{K\ln T}{\eta}+\eta Q_{T,i^*} + K(\ln T)^2)$.

symbols.Q_star: unnormalized variance of best arm's losses

extra_assumptions: eta tuned using knowledge of Q_{T,i*}

source.label: cor:variance_bound
source.quote: With the optimal tuning of $\eta$, the regret is thus of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{KQ_{T,i^*}}+K\right)$.

results.notes: Requires tuning with unknown best-arm variance.

symbols.V_star: first-order path-length of best arm, sum_t |l_{t,i*} - l_{t-1,i*}|

extra_assumptions: eta tuned using knowledge of V_{T,i*}

source.label: thm:path_length
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD+} with $m_{t,i}=\ell_{\alpha_i(t), i}$ and $\eta_{1,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{810}$ guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T] \leq \frac{2K\ln T}{\eta} + \mathbb{E}[\rho_{T+1,i^*}]( \frac{-1}{40\eta\ln T} + 90\eta V_{T,i^*}) + \mathcal{O}(1)$ when $T\geq 3$. Picking $\eta = ...$ leads to $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T] = \tilde{\mathcal{O}}( K\sqrt{V_{T,i^*}}+K )$.

results.notes: Only tuned bound recorded; untuned bound involves random threshold rho.

symbols.K_0: max number of arms in an action

extra_assumptions: conditions (ii) w_{t,i}|hat l - m| <= 3 and (iii) of Theorem 6 hold

source.label: thm:doubling_trick_theorem
source.quote: If conditions (ii) and (iii) in Theorem~\ref{lemma:second_order_regret_bound} hold, then Algorithm \ref{alg:doubling} guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{(K\ln T)\mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^Kw_{t,i}^2(\hat{\ell}_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2]}+K_0K\ln T)$.

results.notes: Parameter-free in eta; T assumed known per appendix.

symbols.V_all: sum over arms of first-order path-lengths sum_i V_{T,i}

source.label: cor:path_length_bound_1
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with $a_{t,i}=0$, $m_{t,i}=\ell_{\alpha_i(t),i}$, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{162}$ guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]\leq\mathcal{O}(\frac{K\ln T}{\eta}) + 6\eta\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i} -\mathbb{E}[...]\leq \mathcal{O}( \frac{K\ln T}{\eta} + \eta\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i})$.

results.notes: Negative stability term dropped in this record.

symbols.V_all: sum over arms of first-order path-lengths sum_i V_{T,i}

source.label: cor:path_length_bound_1
source.quote: Using the doubling trick (Algorithm~\ref{alg:doubling}), we achieve expected regret $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{K\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i}} + K\right)$.

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with $a_t = 0$, $m_{t,i}=\ell_{t,i_t}$, $\hat{\ell}_{t,i}=\frac{\ell_{t,i}\mathbbm{1}\{i_t=i\}}{w_{t,i}}$, and the doubling trick (Algorithm~\ref{alg:doubling}), guarantees \mathbb{E}[\reg_T]=\mathcal{O}(...)

symbols.Delta: fixed conditional expected gap between a* and every other arm

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: This bound implies that in the stochastic setting, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T\right] = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{K\ln T}{\Delta}\right)$

results.notes: Delta is a uniform gap (acts like Delta_min); expectation also over losses.

symbols.L_star: cumulative loss of best arm L_{T,i*}

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: while in the adversarial setting, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T\right] = \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{KL_{T,i^*}\ln T}+K\ln T\right)$ assuming non-negative losses.

extra_assumptions: both players run Broad-OMD as in Corollary 8

source.label: thm:fast_convergence_theorem
source.quote: if both players run \textsc{Broad-OMD} configured as in Corollary~\ref{cor:path_length_bound_1} except that $\eta_{t,i}=\eta= (M+N)^{-\frac{1}{4}}T^{-\frac{1}{4}}$, then their expected average strategies converge to Nash equilibriums at the rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}((M+N)^{\frac{5}{4}}/T^{\frac{3}{4}})$

results.notes: Quantity is duality gap of expected average strategies, not regret.
